To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the methods of direct (1, 2) and indirect (3, 4) methanol determination in pectins are different and that the method of enzymatic demethoxylation and methanol determination is recommended as a selective and precise one.
The methods of direct and indirect methanol determination connected to enzymatic or alkaline pectin demethylations were applied.
the indirect methods of determining methoxyl groups gave higher values of methoxyl group content in commercial pectins.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the comparison of some methods of methoxyl content determination in commercial pectins.
the development of a simple, precise, and selective method for the determination of the degree of methylation of pectin preparations.
the development and comparison of methods for the determination methoxyl groups and the degree of methylation of commercial pectins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the method of direct methanol analysis (I), which does not require the use of expensive equipment, is the most convenient for routine use.
in all the methods applied, the degree of methylation is overestimated.
the method of methanol determination by direct gas-liquid chromatography is recommended for routine analysis of methoxyl content of pectin preparations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the determination of methanol in the presence of other alcohols is possible, but it is not easy.
the determination of methanol in commercial pectins by the direct method (I, II), which is simple and precise, can be recommended.
all the four methods used are precise and selective.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the purity of commercial pectin can only be determined by using a method based on the calculation of DM from the ratio of the methylated carboxylic groups and a total of acidic ones.

it is necessary to determine methoxyl groups using a method based on the direct determination of methanol, and to calculate the purity of peticin based on the difference between the degree of methylation determined by direct and indirect methods.
the determination of DM based on the methanol content is more reliable than that based on the content of methylated carboyl groups.
